scanner_doubts: qe-math-002 x5 in mccall_model_with_separation.md (lines 156, 181, 214, 480, 498) are all false positives. Every one is the next-period prime `w'` in `\sum_{w' \in \mathbb W}` - line 126 states the convention explicitly ('primes denote next period values') - and the lecture has no transposes at all. The `prime_vec` regex in check_math_002 fires on a lowercase letter followed by a prime and then a backslash command, which `w' \in` satisfies; the derivative exception `(?!\s*\()` does not cover next-period primes. This pattern is pervasive in the dynamic-programming lectures, so the same false positive is likely wherever `w' \in`, `x' \in` or `s' \in` appears.

qe-code-003 x1 at line 37 of mccall_model_with_separation.md is a false positive: the install cell at 37-41 runs `!pip install quantecon jax myst-nb` and the flagged import is `myst_nb` (line 68). check_code_003 tests `e.lower() in p.lower()`, so the underscore in the module name never matches the hyphen in the distribution name. Normalising `-` and `_` before the containment test would clear it.
